YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to the regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  September 28, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 6:05 p.m. on
September 28, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan

Mayor Khan announced that City Hall was now open to the public, allowing members of
the public to physically attend and participate in City Council meetings, and noted the
current guidelines for face coverings. She also noted that 1) the meeting was broadcast
live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99,
and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; 2) members of the public would continue to
have the ability to provide live comments on agenda items via Zoom; and 3) the City of
Irvine continued to sanitize surfaces and equipment in the Council Chamber and
throughout City Hall.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to participate in the
meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended, which allowed
members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all agenda items, which
would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s website.

Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Councilmember Kuo provided the invocation.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Commend Chief of Police Mike Hamel in Recognition of His Service to
  the City of Irvine

  Mayor Khan presented a commendation to Chief of Police Mike Hamel in
  recognition of his service to the City of Irvine, and congratulated him on
  his upcoming retirement.

  1.2  Tustin Unified School District Presentation

  Dr. Maggie Villegas, Assistant Superintendent, Educational Services,
  Tustin Unified School District (TUSD), provided a brief presentation on
  TUSD’s background, notable accomplishments, health and safety
  measures during the COVID-19 pandemic, and economic status; and
  expressed appreciation to the City Council for its continued support.

  1.3  Pavement Management Program

  Mark Steuer, Director of Public Works and Transportation, provided a brief
  presentation and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning the percentage of backlog
  and identification of any streets under 70 PSI; questioned the backlog of
  any streets under 70 PCI (Pavement Condition Index) ; inquired about the
  types of vehicles that would operate as part of the ROVER application;
  questioned the pavement standards that other agencies are subject to
  when performing construction on existing roads; questioned whether
  multiple agencies coordinate construction projects on streets; inquired
  about number of miles of paved roads within the City; questioned if any
  pavement products were provided by All American Asphalt; inquired about
  various pavement products on City roads; questioned the requirement for
  rubber; inquired about slurry seal versus a complete rehabilitation;
  questioned what proactive steps the City was taking to prevent additional
  backlogging of roads; and inquired about pavement rehabilitation on
  Trabuco Road.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  1.4  Presentation of the Citywide Strategic Priorities and Corresponding
  Priority Projects

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, and Barbara Arenado,
  Deputy Director of Financial Management & Strategic Planning, provided
  a brief presentation and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquired about the status of unfunded
  pension liability and suggested target percentage; noted investments
  made in environmental sustainability; inquired about the potential financial
  impact of Great Park projects; and suggested that the presentation be
  showcased through the City’s social media platforms.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  Interim City Manager Marysheva provided a brief update on the City’s Mentorship
  Program.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo provided a brief update on his recent trip to the League of
  California Cities Conference and Expo in Sacramento and his recent participation in
  Irvine Feeds the World program with Shepherd’s Grove Church. He also recognized
  Irvine student Aminah Rangwala, who was recently recognized by the Orange County
  Sanitation District for producing a stop motion Public Service Announcement about the
  proper disposal of Fats, Oils, and Grease; and offered his thoughts and prayers to the
  families of Kyu Che, who was tragically killed in a traffic collision, and asked for the
  public’s assistance in identifying witnesses to the accident.

  Vice Mayor Kim also provided a brief update on her recent trip to the League of
  California Cities Conference and Expo in Sacramento; and congratulated Mayor Khan
  for being elected to the Asian Pacific Islander Caucus. She also announced a recent
  trip to Alakazam Comics in Irvine on National Comic Book Day; and provided an update
  on behalf of the Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District on the first
  confirmed case of the West Nile Virus in the City of Buena Park.

  Councilmember Agran reiterated his prior request for support to agendize a
  proclamation for Children’s Environmental Health Month.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The City of Irvine’s strategic priorities continue to focus on five areas of
  importance to the community including Quality of Life, Traffic and Mobility,
  Natural Environment, Fiscal Strength, and Organizational Excellence. Initiatives
  in alignment with these strategic priorities include: 1) a web-based, all-hazard,
  real time evacuation zone map designed to get visual emergency information to
  community members during times of disaster, established by the Office of

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  Emergency Management, 2) a free Green Business Assistance Program to help
  businesses operate sustainably and receive public recognition for their efforts, 3)
  installation of pothole inspection equipment in City vehicles, 4) a number of
  technology solutions for residents, and 5) fostering an environment that is
  inclusive of all cultures, backgrounds, races, and ethnicities as part of the
  Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiative.

  •  Irvine is once again the Safest City of its size for violent crime, recording the
  lowest per capita violent crime rate for all cities in the U.S. with a population over
  250,000, according to FBI data just released for calendar year 2020. It is the 16th
  consecutive year Irvine has recorded the lowest per capita violent crime rate for
  a city its size. Ensuring the safety of residents and visitors, and preserving the
  quality of life for all who come to Irvine, has always been a top priority for the City
  Council. As the City has grown, the City has maintained the highest level of public
  safety that continues to make Irvine an outstanding community to live, work and
  play.

  •  After a relatively quiet 2021 concert season at FivePoint Amphitheatre, the City
  recently saw a spike in noise complaints earlier in the month, with 80% of
  complaints tied to two concerts in particular. The City has been working closely
  with Live Nation, the operator of the venue, to implement changes as soon as
  possible to better control noise levels in the community, which includes adjusting
  placement and direction of amphitheater speakers, enhancing monitoring of the
  speakers and soundboard during concerns, and installing sound absorption
  blankets on the back of and between bleachers. In addition, the City is also
  reviewing its noise ordinance to ensure that the low-end bass tones that have
  generated many of the complaints are properly regulated. Should community
  members experience further noise or disruption during concerts at the
  amphitheater, call the Irvine Police Department Dispatch at 949-724-7000. For
  general information, call Code Enforcement at 949-724-6326.

  •  The 20th annual Irvine Global Village Festival will be held on Saturday, October
  9 from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Great Park. The City’s signature event features
  international cuisine, live entertainment, a Kids Village with crafts and activities,
  cultural and religious exhibits, and an international marketplace. Attendees are
  invited to bring canned food donations for OC Food Bank and UCI Health will be
  providing free flu shots, COVID-19 vaccines, and COVID Boosters while supplies
  last. Those eligible for the COVID Booster will need to bring their vaccine card.
  To volunteer, shifts are available 7:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. Friday, October 8, through
  Sunday, October 10. Volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Irvine Global
  Village Festival is presented by UC Irvine and UCI Health. Festival admission
  and parking are free. For more information about the event or to sign up to
  volunteer, visit irvinefestival.org.

  •  The City of Irvine has once again been voted “Best City to Live In” in Orange
  County. This is the sixth consecutive year that the City has received this honor
  in The Orange County Register’s annual “Best of OC” selections. Winners are
  determined by Register readers, so this recognition is particularly meaningful

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  because many community members took the time to vote for Irvine. The City’s
  schools; public safety; recreation programs; parks and trails; dining and
  shopping; and diversity all provide an unmatched quality of life. As the City
  commemorates its 50th anniversary this year, this recognition offers one more
  reason to celebrate Irvine.

  •  The City of Irvine was one of 11 cities to receive Helen Putnam Awards for
  Excellence from the League of California Cities at its Annual Conference and
  Expo last week. The City received two awards for its efforts to improve the quality
  of life in Irvine and ensure efficient and effective delivery of services. The wildfire
  preparedness efforts, specifically the updated all-hazard evacuation map, was
  recognized as well as IrvineREADY!, the City’s web-based platform that allows
  planning, building, and engineering applications to be submitted online.

  Tony Cardenas, Public Affairs Regional Manager with the League of California
  Cities, presented the Helen Putnam Awards to the City Council on behalf of the
  League of California Cities.

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of Vice
  Mayor Kim, who requested clarification on the proposed term of the lease
  agreement, and questioned whether the City was obligated to pay for any
  capital improvements. Councilmember Carroll also requested clarification
  on the location of the designated Planning Area.

  Joel Belding, Deputy Director of Great Park Planning & Development,
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern about the term and
  monthly lease rate reflected in the proposed agreement; questioned
  whether the City Council had the authority to modify land use; expressed
  concern about the affordable housing shortage; questioned whether the
  Golf Club was a non-profit entity and provided a public benefit; inquired
  about how many unbuilt units were available in Planning Area 21;
  questioned whether the golf course was within County of Orange
  jurisdiction or Irvine Ranch Water District; inquired about the process to
  overturn designated open space; and inquired about the 30-day
  termination clause.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, clarified that land use could be overturned
  through an initiative; however, a separate component included a real
  property deed restriction, and the restriction would have a contractual right
  to require the City to honor it. He also clarified that the right to terminate
  allows for termination on a 10-day notice if the lessee lost the ability to
  operate the golf course; however, if the lease was not renewed and at the
  conclusion of the 10-year term, the agreement would become terminable
  on a 30-day notice.

  4.4  STRATEGIES TO ENCOURAGE WORKFORCE HOUSING

  Lisa Varon, Housing Manager, and Kerwin Lau, Manager of Planning
  Services, presented the staff report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: requesting clarification of the goals of
  workforce housing; expressed concern that the City fell short on
  housing programs for mid-income professionals; inquired about
  funding opportunities available for workforce housing; expressed
  concern about attracting new economic development opportunities if
  workforce housing did not exist; noted high rental costs in the City;
  suggested partnering with the Orange County Business Council to
  advocate housing and workforce development; inquired about options
  the City had to promote local preference for workforce housing; and
  noted developer commitments for additive housing, and suggested that
  staff follow-up with the developer on the status of those units.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that some challenges and
  limitations were identified with respect to local preference, and his
  office would work with staff to update those guidelines.

  Boris Gresely and John Hanna spoke in support of workforce housing
  and living wages for construction workers.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Kim, seconded by Mayor Khan,
  and unanimously carried to:

  Direct staff to return to the City Council with tangible action items
  to assist with workforce housing, which includes funding
  sources, collaboration with outside agencies, and researching
  how the City could keep its employees working and living in the
  City of Irvine.

  4.6  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN AND
  COUNCILMEMBER CARROLL TO DISCUSS COMMERCIAL
  TRUCKS USING CITY OF IRVINE ROADS

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and
  Councilmember Carroll, who expressed concern about commercial
  trucks using City of Irvine roads.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, presented the staff report and responded
  to questions.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  14
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether a separate City
  policy existed that exempts garbage trucks in neighborhoods; inquired
  about the Air Quality Management District’s (AQMD) ability to regulate
  truck coverings based on the California Vehicle Code; questioned why
  the City must permit a commercial truck to enter the City of Irvine;
  inquired about available options, if any, to restrict asphalt trucks from
  using the public right-of-way; questioned whether parking restrictions
  for commercial trucks could be included in an ordinance; inquired
  about whether the City had the authority to designate truck routes;
  questioned whether Code Enforcement could monitor the loading and
  unloading of trucks; inquired about setting up a viable check-point;
  suggested a Code Enforcement hotline be established; inquired about
  a complaint process on behalf of Irvine residents to AQMD; and
  questioned whether the City could restrict or regulate specific
  chemicals.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to emissions generated
  from commercial trucks using City of Irvine roads:

  1) Tom Hazard, Irvine resident
  2) Lesley Tan, Irvine resident
  3) Kim Konte, Irvine resident
  4) Priya Shrivastava, Irvine resident

  Harvey Liss, Irvine resident, spoke in support of mandatory routes for
  covered commercial trucks.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, to:

  1) Review and expand restricted routes that would include parking
  restrictions for commercial vehicles.
  2) Direct staff to return to the City Council with an ordinance on
  disclosures, including new sale, resale, and rental homes.
  3) Through the settlement agreement, require all commercial
  trucks to be covered, and set-up a mechanism to enforce ticket
  violations.
  4) Prepare a letter on behalf of the City Council to California State
  Senator David Min seeking assistance with a list of requests
  related to State legislation to assist the City with this matter, and
  engage with Townsend Public Affairs to strategize further
  development.
  5) Explore the possible relocation of the All American Asphalt
  plant if the City’s options are limited.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  15
 City Council Minutes  September 28, 2021

  ACTION: A friendly amendment was made by Councilmember Agran,
  to:

  1) Review and expand restricted routes that would include parking
  restrictions for commercial vehicles.
  2) Direct staff to return to the City Council with an ordinance on
  disclosures, including new sale, resale, and rental homes.
  3) Through the settlement agreement, require all commercial
  trucks to be covered, and set-up a mechanism to enforce ticket
  violations.
  4) Prepare a letter on behalf of the City Council to California State
